results.description: Uniform +100bp across the curve - the standard rates sensitivity ladder. Severity on this snapshot: 99.64th percentile of 20-day 10Y moves, reached in 18 of 4,966 windows (2022 delivered +258bp over ten months). Uniform by construction, so it reads DV01 rather than curve shape; the front end is not this parallel in practice.

The cross-asset move the sensitivity ladders cannot express: equities down with a vol spike, a flight-to-quality rally that steepens from the front end, the yen bid and the peso sold. Every magnitude is the conditional tail mean over the 50 windows where 20-day SPY sat at or below its 1st percentile - measured co-movement, not a magnitude reused across classes. Regenerate with `python -m risk.jobs.calibrate_stress`.

Every pair down 10% against the dollar. Severity: 99.78th percentile of 20-day EURUSD moves, reached in 11 of 4,966 windows. Uniform across pairs by construction - MXN's measured p99 is half again EUR's - so this reads aggregate FX delta, not relative-value risk.

Broad -20% equity selloff with a +20pt vol bid. Severity: 99.52nd percentile of 20-day SPY moves, reached in 24 of 4,966 windows. Single-name betas are deliberately ignored (NVDA's own p99 is roughly twice SPY's), and rates are left unshocked - see RISK_OFF for what the data says actually happens to rates in an equity selloff.
